_source.description: Major global copper mining and smelting operations
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-copper.pdf); International Copper Study Group (ICSG) statistical yearbook (icsg.org); S&P Global Market Intelligence mine profiles; BHP Annual Report 2023 (bhp.com); Codelco Annual Report 2023 (codelco.com); Freeport-McMoRan Annual Report 2023 (fcx.com); Anglo American Annual Report 2023 (angloamerican.com); Glencore Annual Report 2023 (glencore.com); Antofagasta plc Annual Report 2023 (antofagasta.co.uk); Rio Tinto Annual Report 2023 (riotinto.com); Teck Resources Annual Report 2023 (teck.com); First Quantum Minerals Annual Report 2023 (first-quantum.com); Ivanhoe Mines NI 43-101 Technical Reports (ivanhoemines.com); MMG Limited Annual Report 2023 (mmg.com); CMOC Group Annual Report 2023 (cmoc.com); Southern Copper Corporation Annual Report 2023 (southerncoppercorp.com); KGHM Annual Report 2023 (kghm.com); Barrick Gold Annual Report 2023 (barrick.com); Zijin Mining Annual Report 2023 (zijinmining.com)
_source.license: USGS: public domain; ICSG: subscription data summarized under fair use; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Major copper mining operations worldwide. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, and NI 43-101 technical reports. Capacity figures represent copper metal content in concentrate or cathode. Chile alone accounts for ~24% of global mine production (~5.3M tpa). Global refined copper production ~26M tpa (2023).

_coverage.known_gaps: Numerous small-to-medium copper mines in China (~1.8M tpa aggregate from hundreds of operations); artisanal mining in DRC copper belt; many Indian copper mines not individually listed; small operations across Mexico, Kazakhstan, and Iran

sites.name: Escondida
sites.notes: World's largest copper mine by production. Located in the Atacama Desert at 3,100m elevation. BHP 2023 annual report: ~1.1-1.2M tpa Cu. Includes oxide leach SX-EW and two concentrators.

sites.name: Collahuasi
sites.notes: One of the world's largest copper mines, at 4,400m elevation in the Andes. ~600k tpa Cu production. Concentrator and SX-EW plant.

sites.name: Chuquicamata
sites.notes: Historic copper mine operating since 1915. Transitioned from one of the world's largest open pits to underground block cave mining in 2019. Codelco 2023: ~300-330k tpa Cu.

sites.name: El Teniente
sites.notes: World's largest underground copper mine, ~80km south of Santiago in the Andes. Block cave mining at multiple levels. Operating since 1905. New Mine Level expansion underway.

sites.name: Radomiro Tomic
sites.notes: Large oxide copper deposit near Chuquicamata. SX-EW cathode production plus sulfide concentrator. Part of Codelco's Chuquicamata district.

sites.name: Los Pelambres
sites.notes: Major copper-moly mine in Coquimbo Region. Concentrator expansion completed 2023. Antofagasta 2023: ~370k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Centinela
sites.notes: Merged operation of Esperanza and El Tesoro mines in the Atacama. Produces copper concentrate and cathode. Second concentrator expansion proposed.

sites.name: Spence
sites.notes: Copper mine in the Atacama Desert. Spence Growth Option (SGO) concentrator commissioned 2021 to process sulfide ore. BHP 2023: ~200k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Quebrada Blanca Phase 2 (QB2)
sites.ownership: Teck (60%), Sumitomo Metal Mining / Sumitomo Corp (30%), ENAMI (10%)
sites.notes: Major greenfield copper project at 4,400m elevation. QB2 concentrator commissioned mid-2023, ramping to 300k tpa Cu. One of the largest new copper mines globally.

sites.name: Sierra Gorda
sites.ownership: KGHM (55%), Sumitomo Metal Mining / Sumitomo Corp (45%)
sites.notes: Copper-moly-gold mine in the Atacama. KGHM's flagship international operation. ~120k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Cerro Verde
sites.ownership: Freeport-McMoRan (53.56%), SMM Cerro Verde (21%), Compania de Minas Buenaventura (19.58%), others (5.86%)
sites.notes: Peru's largest copper mine, near Arequipa. Massive concentrator expansion completed 2015. Freeport 2023: ~470-500k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Antamina
sites.notes: World-class polymetallic skarn deposit at 4,300m in the Andes. One of the highest-grade large copper mines. ~470k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Las Bambas
sites.ownership: MMG Limited (62.5%), a consortium of CITIC Metal and others (37.5%)
sites.notes: Major copper mine in Apurimac region, southern Peru. Acquired by MMG from Glencore in 2014. Has faced community blockade disruptions to logistics corridor.

sites.name: Quellaveco
sites.notes: Anglo American's $5.5B greenfield copper mine in Moquegua. First production mid-2022, ramped to ~300k tpa Cu in 2023. One of the newest major copper mines globally.

sites.name: Toromocho
sites.notes: Chinese-owned porphyry copper mine at 4,500m in Junin region. Expansion completed 2020 to double throughput. ~250k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Cuajone
sites.notes: Open-pit porphyry copper mine in Moquegua, southern Peru. Operating since 1976. Southern Copper 2023: ~150k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Kamoa-Kakula
sites.ownership: Ivanhoe Mines (39.6%), Zijin Mining (39.6%), Crystal River (0.8%), DRC Government (20%)
sites.notes: World-class copper discovery in the Katanga copper belt. Among the highest-grade major copper deposits. Phase 1-3 concentrators operational. Ivanhoe 2023: ~394k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Tenke Fungurume
sites.notes: Major copper-cobalt operation in Katanga. CMOC 2023: ~300k tpa Cu, ~30k tpa Co. SX-EW copper cathode and cobalt hydroxide.

sites.name: Mutanda
sites.notes: Large Cu-Co mine restarted in 2022 after 2019 suspension. Glencore 2023: ~170-200k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Kamoto (KCC)
sites.notes: Historic Cu-Co complex in Kolwezi. Glencore 2023: ~250k tpa Cu, ~25k tpa Co.

sites.name: Morenci
sites.ownership: Freeport-McMoRan (72%), Sumitomo Metal Mining (15%), Sumitomo Corp (13%)
sites.notes: Largest copper mine in North America, located in southeastern Arizona. Open-pit mining with SX-EW and concentrator. Freeport 2023: ~450k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Bingham Canyon (Kennecott)
sites.notes: Historic open-pit mine near Salt Lake City, Utah. One of the world's deepest open pits. Operating since 1906. Smelter and refinery on-site. ~200k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Bagdad
sites.notes: Porphyry copper mine in Yavapai County, Arizona. Concentrator and SX-EW operations. ~100k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Resolution
sites.notes: One of the world's largest undeveloped copper deposits, near Superior, Arizona. Would be one of the largest US copper mines at ~450k tpa Cu. Permitting delayed by land-exchange controversy (Apache sacred site at Oak Flat). Deep block cave at ~2,000m depth.

sites.name: Grasberg
sites.notes: World's largest gold mine and second-largest copper mine by reserves. Transitioned from open pit to underground block cave (Grasberg Block Cave and Deep Mill Level Zone). Located in Papua at ~4,200m elevation. Freeport 2023: ~600k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Kansanshi
sites.notes: Africa's largest copper mine by production. Mixed oxide-sulfide orebody. S3 expansion underway to increase to ~400k tpa. First Quantum 2023: ~220-250k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Sentinel
sites.notes: Greenfield copper mine in Northwestern Province. One of the largest single-line copper concentrators. First Quantum 2023: ~250-270k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Lumwana
sites.notes: Large open-pit copper mine in Zambia's Northwestern Province. Super Pit Expansion project underway to extend mine life and increase production. Barrick 2023: ~120-130k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Olympic Dam
sites.notes: World's largest known uranium deposit, fourth-largest copper deposit. IOCG (iron oxide copper gold) orebody. Underground sub-level open stoping. BHP 2023: ~180-200k tpa Cu. Also produces ~3,500 tpa U3O8.

sites.name: Cadia Valley
sites.notes: One of Australia's largest gold-copper operations near Orange, NSW. Panel cave mining (Cadia East). ~55k tpa Cu as byproduct of gold mining.

sites.name: Prominent Hill
sites.notes: IOCG deposit in South Australia. Transitioned from open pit to underground. Acquired via BHP's 2023 takeover of OZ Minerals. ~80-90k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Oyu Tolgoi
sites.ownership: Turquoise Hill/Rio Tinto (66%), Government of Mongolia (34%)
sites.notes: World-class porphyry copper-gold deposit in the South Gobi desert. Hugo North underground block cave (Lift 1) achieved sustainable production in 2023. Will become one of the world's top four copper mines at full underground production (~500k tpa Cu).

sites.name: Erdenet
sites.notes: Mongolia's oldest and second-largest copper mine, operating since 1978. ~130k tpa Cu. State-owned joint venture.

sites.name: Cobre Panama
sites.ownership: First Quantum Minerals (90%), Korea Panama Mining Corp (10%)
sites.notes: One of the world's newest large copper mines. Panama Supreme Court ruled the mining concession unconstitutional in Nov 2023; mine placed on preservation and safe management. ~330-350k tpa Cu when operating.

sites.name: Udokan
sites.notes: Russia's largest undeveloped copper deposit in Zabaykalsky Krai. Phase 1 commissioned late 2022. One of the world's largest copper deposits by reserves (~26.7M t Cu). ~135k tpa at full Phase 1; Phase 2 will double output.

sites.name: Malmyzh
sites.notes: Large porphyry copper-gold deposit in Khabarovsk Krai, Russian Far East. Under development by Russian Copper Company. ~250k tpa Cu planned.

sites.name: KGHM Polkowice-Sieroszowice / Rudna / Lubin
sites.ownership: KGHM Polska Miedz (31.8% Polish state treasury)
sites.notes: KGHM operates three underground mines in the Legnica-Glogow Copper District (LGCD). One of Europe's largest copper producers. Very deep mining (1,000-1,200m). KGHM 2023: ~390k tpa Cu. Major silver byproduct (~40M oz/yr).

sites.name: Toquepala
sites.notes: Porphyry copper mine in Tacna, southern Peru. Concentrator expansion completed 2018 doubled capacity. Southern Copper 2023: ~290-300k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Buenavista del Cobre (Cananea) / La Caridad
sites.notes: Mexico's largest copper mining complex in Sonora state. Includes Buenavista (formerly Cananea) and La Caridad mines plus smelter/refinery. Southern Copper 2023: ~490-500k tpa Cu combined.

sites.name: Salobo
sites.notes: IOCG copper-gold deposit in Carajas mineral province, Para state. Three processing lines. Vale 2023: ~180-200k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Sossego
sites.notes: IOCG copper-gold mine in Carajas, Para state. Vale 2023: ~90-100k tpa Cu.

sites.name: Los Bronces
sites.notes: Large porphyry copper mine in the Andes above Santiago. Anglo American 2023: ~180-200k tpa Cu. Integrated development plan with nearby underground resources.

sites.name: Dexing
sites.notes: China's largest open-pit copper mine, in Jiangxi province. Operating since 1958. Jiangxi Copper is China's largest copper producer. ~180k tpa Cu mine production.

sites.name: Zijinshan (Zijin Gold-Copper Mine)
sites.notes: Flagship gold-copper mine of Zijin Mining in Fujian province. Bioleaching copper recovery. ~80k tpa Cu.
